nodes.label: CQRS
nodes.rationale: Separates command and query code paths without requiring event sourcing, separate databases, or distributed messaging.

nodes.label: Layer Dependency Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Keeps Application contracts independent of HTTP and persistence frameworks, with bootstrap as the sole composition point for Infrastructure.

nodes.label: In-Process Notifications
nodes.rationale: MediatR notifications are immediate and non-durable; critical publication requires a transactional outbox and idempotent consumer.

nodes.label: Feature-by-Feature Migration
nodes.rationale: Allows existing services and controllers to remain operational until replacement endpoints preserve contracts and pass integration tests.

nodes.label: Six-Project Module Template
nodes.rationale: Every deployable business area uses the same template from its first commit.

nodes.label: NuGet Central Package Management
nodes.rationale: A single ERP package-version policy provides consistent versions without silently changing independent applications.

nodes.label: Database Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Each module owns one DbContext, migrations assembly, default SQL schema, and EF migrations history table that no other module touches.

nodes.label: One Schema Per Module
nodes.rationale: There is no feature sub-schema by default.

nodes.label: MoveHrTablesToHrSchema Migration
nodes.rationale: The migration moves all HR tables, including Identity, from dbo to hr through pure renames with no data loss.

nodes.label: HR Bootstrap Legacy Migration History Transfer
nodes.rationale: The HR bootstrap ensures hr exists, transfers dbo history only when hr history is absent and dbo history exists, then runs MigrateAsync.

nodes.label: Idempotent Startup Migration
nodes.rationale: New-module bootstraps ensure schemas before inspecting migrations and make startup migration idempotent.
